title: Turf Replacement in the Denver Metro | TIMELESS Grass & Greens
description: Replace worn artificial turf in the Denver metro. New turf must be PFAS-free since 2026, some cities set replacement and base rules, and HOA land has its own test.
h1: Replace worn turf with new turf built to 2026 rules.
lede: Pull up turf that has flattened, stopped draining or no longer looks like a lawn, and put down turf that meets the rules in force now. Since 2026 that means PFAS-free turf anywhere in Colorado, and some metro cities add their own replacement, base and permit rules. We check the ground at a free visit and give you a custom layout to approve before work starts.
wins: Know what Colorado's 2026 PFAS rule means for the new turf
Know your city's replacement and base rules before you commit
A base built for your soil before the new turf goes down

answer.question: Can I replace old artificial turf in the Denver metro?
answer.answer: Yes. Colorado law doesn't stop you maintaining turf installed before 1 January 2026, but since that date no one may install artificial turf containing intentionally added PFAS chemicals on any property in the state, so the new turf has to meet that rule. Some metro cities also set their own turf standards, and on HOA or business land a replacement can count as redevelopment. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

blocks.h2: The turf going back in has to be PFAS-free.
paras: Since 1 January 2026, Colorado law says a person shall not install artificial turf that contains intentionally added PFAS chemicals on any portion of property in the state (SB24-081). That reaches your back yard as well as business and HOA land. The same section says nothing in it prohibits maintaining artificial turf installed before that date.

So an older lawn can stay, but the turf that replaces it is new turf going in. Before you approve a product, ask for written documentation that it has no intentionally added PFAS, and ask whether that covers the backing and infill as well as the fibers. Our PFAS article covers the background.

Thornton Water's 2026 turf rules for its water-wise landscape rebate ask for more. All turf, infill and other products used to install it must be PFAS-free, the documentation goes in with the permit application, and a "PFC-free" statement isn't enough (Thornton Water).

blocks.h2: Some metro cities say when worn turf must be replaced.
paras: Northglenn's development code lists replacement among the required upkeep for artificial turf: "replacement of the artificial turf when maintenance or repair is unable to simulate a healthy living turf" (Northglenn Municipal Code). Thornton Water's 2026 rules use nearly the same line. Brighton's plant specifications say turf "shall be replaced when it is no longer simulating the infiltration properties of sod or native grasses" (City of Brighton).

Where those standards apply, turf that no longer looks or drains like a lawn is due for replacement under the code. Northglenn's section applies to new development and land uses and to some expansions, so ask the planning office whether it covers your property, and bring any letter from the city to the visit. We read these codes in September 2026; ask for the current version before you plan. The Northglenn, Brighton and Thornton pages cover the rest of each city's rules.

Boulder's landscape manual works the other way. Its turf section says landscaping installed before 7 March 2026 "may be maintained and is not required to comply with these provisions", unless a project or change to the site requires compliance (City of Boulder). Ask the city whether your replacement is maintenance or a change.

blocks.h2: Build the new base to today's standard, not the old one.
paras: Replacement is when you find out what's under the old turf. Where Northglenn's section applies, sod or existing groundcover comes off first, the turf goes over compacted, porous road base, every edge and seam is anchored, and turf can't go on a slope steeper than six percent. Brighton requires the turf and any underlayment to percolate at least 5 inches an hour. Thornton's rules call for at least three inches of compacted aggregate that takes half an inch of rain before water runs off the surface.

A base laid years ago may not meet those standards, and some of it only shows once the rolls are up. At the free visit we measure, check the ground and the slope, and plan site prep and a base built for your soil. Agree before work starts how anything found after removal is priced and approved. Our article on what goes under artificial turf explains the layers.

blocks.h2: On shared or business land, ask whether the job counts as redevelopment.
paras: From 1 January 2026, Colorado bars cities, counties, towns, special districts and metropolitan districts from installing or allowing nonfunctional artificial turf in a new development or redevelopment project on commercial, institutional or industrial property, HOA common property, or a street right-of-way, parking lot or median (SB24-005, as amended by HB25-1113). A single-family lot isn't on that list. Shared grounds in larger multifamily housing have a date question of their own, covered below.

The law doesn't stop turf installed before that date from being maintained, and it defines maintaining as an action to preserve the existing state of turf already installed. It doesn't say whether stripping and relaying a whole area counts. A replacement is a redevelopment project only if it needs a building or landscaping permit, plan check or design review and disturbs more than half of the aggregate landscape area.

If it is, use decides what can go back. The law describes functional artificial turf as turf in an area regularly used for civic, community or recreational purposes, which may include a playground, a sports field, a picnic ground, a portion of a park and the playing area of a golf course. A local government or district can also set stricter rules. Ask the planning office, and any district that reviews the land, how it will class your job, and get the answer in writing. Our Colorado turf law guide has the full text.

blocks.h2: Bring what the city and your association have sent you.
paras: Bring photos of where the old turf is flat, lumpy or holding water, any letter from the city or association, and the original installation details if you have them. For HOA or business land, add the landscape plan and the total landscaped area, so the redevelopment question can be settled before you commit.

On the free visit we measure and check the ground. You get a custom layout to approve before work starts, then site prep, a base built for your soil, new turf laid, seamed and edged, infill, finishing and cleanup, and a walkthrough of the care it needs. Start from the turf replacement service or the Denver metro page.

faq.q: Do I have to pull up turf installed before 2026?
faq.a: Not because of state law. The PFAS law and the state turf law both say they don't prohibit maintaining turf installed before 1 January 2026. A city code can still call for worn turf to be replaced, as Northglenn's and Brighton's do where they apply, so ask your planning office how its code treats existing turf.

faq.q: Does Thornton's turf rebate cover replacing old artificial turf?
faq.a: Not as its 2026 rules are written. To qualify, the turf must replace high-water lawn such as Kentucky bluegrass on an existing lot, or ground with no landscaping on a new-construction lot. Old artificial turf isn't on that list, so ask Thornton Water before you count on a payment.

faq.q: Can an HOA replace turf on a playground or sports area?
faq.a: State law doesn't stop artificial turf on athletic fields of play, and its description of functional artificial turf may include a playground or a sports field. Your city or district can set stricter rules. Describe the use on any plan you submit and ask for the classification in writing.

faq.q: Does the 2028 date affect an apartment community?
faq.a: It can reach the shared grounds. HB25-1113 adds a 1 January 2028 date for common interest property, such as entryways, parks and other common elements, in multifamily housing with more than twelve dwelling units. If you manage a rental complex rather than an association, ask whether your grounds count. Published guidance also disagrees on the date, as our HOA turf guide explains, so ask your municipality which date and standards it has adopted.

faq.q: Can old turf be recycled in the Denver area?
faq.a: Don't assume it. When we checked in September 2026, the accepted-materials list at Boulder's Center for Hard-to-Recycle Materials had no turf or carpet category (Eco-Cycle/City of Boulder CHaRM). Ask where the old turf and infill will go before work starts.
